title: Gender Bender Noun Disaster (Der Die Das Drop)
style: chaotic electronic comedy, 128 BPM, glitchy drops, cartoon sound effects, vocoder stutter, big synth bass, breakbeats, robotic spoken interludes, German techno influence, EN/ES/DE codeswitch, gameshow buzzer, manic energy, hooky chorus
lyrics:
[Intro — glitchy electronic build, cartoon "boing" SFX]
Warning, warning, gender error
Noun mismatch detected
Brain.exe has stopped responding
[BOOM]

[Verse 1 — chaotic, high energy]
El problema is MASCULINE — wait, ends in -A!
La solución is FEMININE — what is this, what?
In German "das Mädchen" means "the GIRL" but it's NEUTRAL
Grammar is trolling us, send help, this is lethal!

[Pre-Chorus — glitchy stutter]
Der die das, der die das, der die das DROP
El la los las, el la los las, el la los STOP
The endings lie, the endings lie, the rules forget to apply
Gender bender, send help, send help, oh my!

[Chorus — full electronic freakout]
Why is a TABLE masculine in some Spanish dreams?
La mesa — wait — feminine — never what it seems!
Der Tisch, die Lampe, das Chaos in my brain
Gender bender, send help, por favor, again!

[Verse 2 — example-rap, rapid-fire]
"El agua" — el? But agua's feminine? YES
The rule says "feminine nouns starting with stressed A
take EL in the singular but LAS in the plural"
Las aguas — see? Make it make sense, neural!

[Verse 3 — German chaos]
"Die Sonne" the sun is FEMALE, "der Mond" the moon is MALE
In Spanish flip it backwards — el sol, la luna, fail!
"Das Auto" is neutral, "der Wagen" same car is masculine
What's the difference? NOTHING! That's the German discipline!

[Bridge — robotic spoken]
Rule one: there are no rules
Rule two: see rule one
Rule three: memorize the article with the noun
Rule four: cry, then continue

[Final Chorus]
Why is a TABLE masculine in some Spanish dreams?
La mesa — wait — feminine — never what it seems!
Der Tisch, die Lampe, das Chaos in my brain
Gender bender, send help, por favor, again!

[Outro — exhausted]
El, la, der, die, das… I quit. I QUIT.
